claim: Realtime WebSocket transport_config max_size: the SDK default is None, leaving incoming message size unlimited.
explanation: The realtime connection always starts with connect_kwargs max_size set to 8 * 1024 * 1024 and only overrides it if transport_config supplies max_size. The default is therefore an 8 MiB limit, not unlimited. (The unlimited default is true only for the Responses websocket transport, which sets max_size None.)

claim: By default, UnixLocalSandboxClient starts every command environment from the complete host process environment.
explanation: UnixLocalSandboxClient.__init__ defaults inherit_host_environment to False. In that case _host_environment_allowlist is set to the conservative _HOST_ENVIRONMENT_ALLOWLIST (PATH, LANG, LC_*, TZ, and so on), so host variables outside the allowlist are not passed. Full inheritance is opt-in, the opposite of what the docs say.

claim: Local ShellTool and ApplyPatchTool default to needs_approval=False.
explanation: ApplyPatchTool.needs_approval defaults to False (tool.py:1553), but ShellTool.needs_approval defaults to True (tool.py:1498). Local shell calls therefore require approval by default.

claim: For local ShellTool and ApplyPatchTool, approval is opt-in: needs_approval defaults to False.
explanation: Same discrepancy: ShellTool declares needs_approval: bool | ShellApprovalFunction = True, so approval is opt-out for local shell. Only ApplyPatchTool defaults to False.

claim: Retries are opt in. The SDK does not retry general model requests unless you set ModelSettings(retry=...) and your retry policy chooses to retry.
explanation: With no retry settings, _should_disable_provider_managed_retries returns False on the initial attempt (and on later attempts when there is no policy), so the underlying OpenAI client's built-in retries stay active. The code comments say provider retries are the only transient-failure recovery in that case. Model requests are therefore retried by default; only the runner-managed retry layer is opt-in.
